Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

paragraphs.text: 29. NOTICES

29.1 Legal notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by nationally recognized overnight courier or certified mail, return receipt requested, to the address in the preamble and by email to the legal-notice address stated in the applicable Order Form. Operational notices may be delivered through agreed service channels.

29.2 Notice is effective on documented delivery, except a refusal is deemed delivery. A Party may change its notice address by notice under this Section. Email alone is insufficient for breach, termination, indemnity, assignment, or litigation notices unless receipt is affirmatively acknowledged.
29.3 Notices to Customer must copy legal@northwind.example, and notices to Vendor must copy legal@brightline.example. Automated portal messages, invoices, and website postings are not legal notices.
29.4 The notice period referenced in Section 9.4 is thirty days before the effective termination date and may be given by the methods in Section 29.1.
8. TERM AND RENEWAL

8.1 This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms. Expiration of this Agreement does not itself terminate an Order Form then in effect; this Agreement continues to govern that Order Form until the Order Form expires or is terminated.

8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.

8.3 On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

paragraphs.text: 13. ACCESS RIGHTS AND LICENCE

13.1 Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.

13.2 For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.

13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.

13.4 Customer shall not knowingly reverse engineer hosted source code except to the extent a restriction is prohibited by Applicable Law, interfere with the Services, bypass documented security controls, or use the Services to violate Applicable Law. These restrictions do not limit testing authorized by the security exhibit or use of Customer Data and output.
15. CUSTOMER DATA AND PRIVACY

15.1 Vendor shall process Customer Data only on Customer's documented instructions, to provide the Services, and as permitted by this Agreement. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data, use it for advertising, combine it with another customer's identifiable data, or train a generally available model on it without Customer's express written consent.

15.2 Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law concerning personal information. If Vendor processes personal information for Customer, the Parties' data-processing addendum is incorporated. Vendor is a processor or service provider and shall assist Customer with data-subject requests, impact assessments, consultations, and regulatory inquiries.

Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

paragraphs.text: 13. ACCESS RIGHTS AND LICENCE

13.1 Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.

13.2 For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.

13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.

13.4 Customer shall not knowingly reverse engineer hosted source code except to the extent a restriction is prohibited by Applicable Law, interfere with the Services, bypass documented security controls, or use the Services to violate Applicable Law. These restrictions do not limit testing authorized by the security exhibit or use of Customer Data and output.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

input.rationale: Renewals meet the preferred position in full: renewal terms are 12 months (not multi-year), Customer may opt out on only 30 days' written notice, Vendor must send a renewal reminder 60 days beforehand (with the opt-out deadline extended if it fails to do so), and § 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods. The three-year duration in § 8.1 is the initial term of the master agreement, not an automatic multi-year renewal, so the walk-away trigger is not engaged. No conflicting escalation language appears in § 7. No redline needed.

paragraphs.text: 30. GENERAL

30.1 The Parties are independent contractors. Nothing creates a partnership, joint venture, fiduciary relationship, franchise, or agency. Neither Party may bind the other. Vendor is solely responsible for compensation, direction, and taxes of its personnel.

30.2 Neither Party's failure or delay in exercising a right waives it. A waiver must be written and signed by an authorized representative and applies only to the stated instance. Remedies are cumulative unless an exclusive remedy is expressly identified.

30.3 If a court finds a provision unenforceable, it will be modified to the minimum extent needed to make it enforceable while preserving intent, and the remainder continues. Headings aid reference only. “Including” means “including without limitation,” and “or” is inclusive.

30.4 This Agreement, its exhibits, and executed Order Forms are the entire agreement about their subject and supersede prior proposals, statements, and agreements. An amendment must be in a writing signed by authorized representatives of both Parties and expressly identify this Agreement.

30.5 No person other than a Party, a Customer Affiliate ordering Services, a permitted successor, or an indemnified party has a right to enforce this Agreement. The Parties may amend or terminate it without another person's consent, subject to vested indemnity rights.

30.6 This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, each treated as an original, and by electronic signature. An electronic copy is effective as an original. Each signatory represents that they are authorized to bind the named Party.

30.7 Vendor shall not use an artificial-intelligence system to make a legally binding decision for Customer or submit Customer Confidential Information to a third-party model unless an Order Form expressly authorizes that use and specifies safeguards. Vendor remains responsible for output used in providing the Services.
30.8 The Parties have caused their authorized representatives to execute this Agreement as of the Effective Date.

ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.

Category: assignment

Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.

Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

paragraphs.text: 1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 “Affiliate” means, with respect to a Party, any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Party. “Control” means ownership of more than fifty percent of the voting interests of an entity or the power to direct its management. An entity is an Affiliate only while that relationship continues.

1.2 “Applicable Law” means every statute, regulation, binding regulatory requirement, court order, and governmental rule applicable to a Party's performance under this Agreement, including laws concerning privacy, information security, export controls, employment, anti-bribery, and accessibility. Applicable Law does not include a private standard unless an Order Form expressly adopts it.

1.3 “Customer Data” means all data, records, files, content, personal information, and other materials submitted to, stored in, transmitted through, or otherwise made available to the Services by or for Customer or its Authorized Users, together with output specifically derived from that material. Customer Data excludes anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer, an Authorized User, or an individual.

1.4 “Deliverable” means each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material, and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer. Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.
1.5 “Fees” means the Implementation Fee.
1.6 “Implementation Fee” means the one-time implementation charge of USD 12,000 stated in the first Order Form.

1.7 “Order Form” means a written ordering document signed by authorized representatives of both Parties that references this Agreement and describes the Services, Deliverables, subscription quantities, service levels, Fees, and term purchased by Customer. A purchase order is an administrative convenience only and does not amend an Order Form or this Agreement.

1.8 “Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.

1.9 “Vendor Technology” means Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates, documentation, routines, connectors, and other technology, and modifications of them that are not Deliverables and do not embody Customer Confidential Information. Vendor Technology does not include Customer Data or intellectual property owned by Customer before the Effective Date.

paragraphs.text: 4. ORDER FORMS AND AFFILIATE ORDERS

4.1 An Order Form becomes binding when signed by both Parties. Vendor shall not charge for work outside scope that Customer did not approve in a signed change order.
24. ASSIGNMENT AND CHANGE OF CONTROL

24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.

24.2 Vendor may not assign this Agreement, delegate material performance, or transfer it by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld for an assignee with adequate capability and financial standing. Vendor may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without Customer's consent.

24.3 For other assignments, neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. A permitted assignment does not relieve accrued obligations. An attempted assignment contrary to this Section is void to the extent permitted by law.

24.4 Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service. Vendor shall cooperate with reasonable administrative changes needed to reflect a permitted successor.

Section 7 contains no competing escalation or uplift mechanism, and a document-wide search for "renew"/"increase" surfaced no other renewal terms.

paragraphs.text: 7. FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES

7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.

7.2 Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.

7.3 Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.

7.4 Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.

7.5 Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.
7.6 Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms.

7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.

input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
input.rationale: Section 24 meets the preferred position in full: 24.1 gives Customer an unqualified right to assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor without Vendor consent (notice only); 24.2 bars Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without Customer's consent (reasonableness standard running in our favour) and bars assignment to a direct Customer competitor; 24.3 applies a mutual not-unreasonably-withheld standard to other assignments; and 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on Customer's change of control, with a cooperation obligation for successor administrative changes. Searches for "assign" and "change of control" across the document found no competing trigger — Section 9 termination contains only a standard mutual insolvency/general-assignment-for-creditors right, and Section 13.x confirms Customer may transfer licence rights to an Affiliate or successor under a Section 24 permitted assignment. content.text: Section 24 fully matches our preferred position, and no conflicting change-of-control trigger exists elsewhere.

input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
input.rationale: Section 24 meets the preferred position in full: 24.1 gives Customer an unqualified right to assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor without Vendor consent (notice only); 24.2 bars Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without Customer's consent (reasonableness standard running in our favour) and bars assignment to a direct Customer competitor; 24.3 applies a mutual not-unreasonably-withheld standard to other assignments; and 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on Customer's change of control, with a cooperation obligation for successor administrative changes. Searches for "assign" and "change of control" across the document found no competing trigger — Section 9 termination contains only a standard mutual insolvency/general-assignment-for-creditors right, and Section 13.x confirms Customer may transfer licence rights to an Affiliate or successor under a Section 24 permitted assignment. "Affiliate" (1.1) uses a conventional >50% control test, so the carve-out is not artificially narrow. No redline needed.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline required.

Section 28 already matches our preferred position:
- **§ 28.1** — governed by the laws of the State of New York (with CISG expressly excluded).
- **§ 28.2** — exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, with irrevocable submission to personal jurisdiction.

No arbitration provision exists anywhere in the agreement, and there is no competing governing-law or forum language in any other section, so the walk-away risk (UK home-jurisdiction venue or a foreign-seated arbitration) does not arise notwithstanding that Brightline is a UK entity. The mutual carve-out for temporary injunctive relief and the pre-filing executive escalation (which expressly does not delay urgent relief or limitations-period filings) are both customary and acceptable.

22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 24 already delivers our preferred ASSIGN position on all four elements:

- **24.1** — Customer may assign without Vendor consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets (prompt notice + assignee assumption only).
- **24.2** — Vendor may not assign, delegate material performance, or transfer by change of control without our prior written consent (not unreasonably withheld), and never to a direct Customer competitor.
- **24.3** — Mutual not-unreasonably-withheld/conditioned/delayed standard for other assignments.
- **24.4** — Customer's change of control gives Vendor **no** right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service, plus a cooperation duty for successor administrative changes.

Cross-checks confirmed no hidden conflict: searches for "assign" and "change of control" surfaced nothing adverse; Section 9's only assignment-related termination right is the standard mutual insolvency/general-assignment-for-creditors trigger; Section 13 reinforces that licence rights travel to an Affiliate or successor under a Section 24 permitted assignment; and the Section 1.1 "Affiliate" definition uses a conventional >50% control test, so the carve-out is not artificially narrowed.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

input.quote: 13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.
input.rationale: Section 13 satisfies every element of the preferred position. Clause 13.1 grants the subscription access right to "Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf" on a worldwide, non-exclusive basis for internal business purposes, and extends to Authorized Users — so affiliates and contractors are expressly in scope with no need for the fallback notice mechanic. Clause 13.2 makes paid-up and Deliverable-embedded software a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence" to Customer and its Affiliates, including modification and derivative-work rights and contractor support. Clause 13.3 confirms transferability to an Affiliate or successor via Section 24, and limits revocation or suspension to a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity — i.e., no revocation at Vendor's discretion. Section 24.1 backs this up by allowing Customer to assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor without Vendor's consent, and 24.4 bars Vendor from terminating, repricing, or reducing service on a Customer change of control. The "Affiliate" definition (1.1) is a standard majority-control test that does not narrow the grant. The restrictions in 13.4 are ordinary anti-misuse covenants and are expressly carved back for authorized security testing and Customer Data and output, so they do not undercut the grant. No deviation from the licence-scope rule.

input.quote: 13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.
input.rationale: Section 13 satisfies every element of the preferred position. Clause 13.1 grants the subscription access right to "Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf" on a worldwide, non-exclusive basis for internal business purposes, and extends to Authorized Users — so affiliates and contractors are expressly in scope with no need for the fallback notice mechanic. Clause 13.2 makes paid-up and Deliverable-embedded software a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence" to Customer and its Affiliates, including modification and derivative-work rights and contractor support. Clause 13.3 confirms transferability to an Affiliate or successor via Section 24, and limits revocation or suspension to a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity — i.e., no revocation at Vendor's discretion. Section 24.1 backs this up by allowing Customer to assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor without Vendor's consent, and 24.4 bars Vendor from terminating, repricing, or reducing service on a Customer change of control. The "Affiliate" definition (1.1) is a standard majority-control test that does not narrow the grant. The restrictions in 13.4 are ordinary anti-misuse covenants and are expressly carved back for authorized security testing and Customer Data and output, so they do not undercut the grant. No deviation from the licence-scope rule.

paragraphs.text: 7. FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES

7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.

7.2 Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.

7.3 Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.

7.4 Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.

7.5 Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.
7.6 Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms.

7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
9. TERMINATION

9.1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail. If a breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, the cure period extends up to sixty additional days while the breaching Party diligently pursues cure.

9.2 Either Party may terminate immediately by written notice if the other becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for creditors, enters liquidation, or becomes subject to a bankruptcy proceeding not dismissed within sixty days. A lawful reorganization that does not impair performance is not, by itself, grounds for termination.

9.3 Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.

9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.

9.5 Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.

ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.

"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 13 already delivers the full preferred position on licence scope:

- **Affiliates and contractors covered** — §13.1 grants subscription access to "Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf," plus Authorized Users. No need to fall back to an affiliate-on-notice mechanic.
- **Paid-up licences perpetual and irrevocable** — §13.2 grants a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence" for delivered software and Deliverable-embedded Vendor Technology, including modification and derivative-work rights and contractor support.
- **No revocation at will** — §13.3 permits revocation or suspension only during a material uncured payment or use breach, after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity.
- **Transferable to successors** — §13.3 read with §24.1 allows assignment to an Affiliate or M&A successor without Vendor consent, and §24.4 blocks Vendor from terminating, repricing, or reducing service on our change of control.

The §13.4 use restrictions are ordinary anti-misuse covenants and are expressly carved back for authorized security testing and for Customer Data and output, so they do not erode the grant. The "Affiliate" definition (§1.1) is a standard majority-control test that does not narrow coverage.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 9 already delivers our preferred T4C position without amendment:

| Playbook element | Document | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Customer convenience right | § 9.4 — Agreement *and* any Order Form | Met |
| 30 days' notice | § 29.4 — thirty days | Met |
| Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees | § 9.4 — accrued Fees only + refund | Met |
| No early-termination fee | None in §§ 7, 9, 10 | Met |
| No Vendor mid-term convenience right | Only for-cause (§§ 9.1, 9.2) | Met |

Two points worth noting for the wider review, outside this rule's scope:

1. **§ 9.4 relies on a remote cross-reference.** The 30-day period sits in the Notices section (§ 29.4) rather than in the termination clause itself. It is legally effective as drafted, so I did not flag it — but if you want belt-and-braces protection against a future amendment to § 29 inadvertently diluting our exit right, stating "thirty (30) days' prior written notice" directly in § 9.4 would be a cheap, non-controversial tidy-up.
2. **§ 7.7 is a genuinely aggressive term.** It imposes "fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week" an invoice remains unpaid, labelled liquidated damages. That compounds to an extreme figure and is likely unenforceable as a penalty, but it is a payment-terms issue rather than an early-termination charge, so it does not affect this rule's outcome. It should be picked up under the payment/late-fee rule if one is in scope.

paragraphs.text: 21. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.

21.2 Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill, to the extent those damages are legally excludable. Costs of restoring Customer Data, obtaining replacement services, required notices, and reasonable incident response are direct damages.

21.3 “Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property. Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section.

21.4 The limitations allocate risk between sophisticated Parties and apply only to the maximum extent permitted by Applicable Law. Nothing limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited. Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.

paragraphs.text: 6. ACCEPTANCE

6.1 Customer will have fifteen business days after delivery of a Deliverable to test it against the acceptance criteria in the applicable Order Form. 3.1 Vendor shall provide the Services professionally, diligently, and in accordance with this Agreement, each Order Form, the documentation, agreed project plans, and Applicable Law. Vendor is responsible for the acts and omissions of its personnel, Affiliates, and subcontractors as though they were Vendor's own.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

18.1 Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.

18.2 Policies will be issued by reputable insurers and be primary to Customer's insurance where commercially customary. On request, Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance and evidence of relevant coverage. Vendor shall give advance notice of cancellation or material reduction to the extent available from its insurer. Insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities.

Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

paragraphs.text: 11. TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND DATA RETURN

11.1 Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form. Assistance includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, orderly migration, and continued service at the then-current scope and service levels.

11.2 Within thirty days after Customer's request, Vendor shall return all Customer Data in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format, with relationships and metadata reasonably necessary for use. Vendor shall not withhold Customer Data because of a fee dispute.

11.3 After Customer confirms successful return, Vendor shall securely delete remaining Customer Data from active systems and, as backups cycle, from backups, except for a copy required by Applicable Law. An authorized officer shall certify deletion in writing. Any retained copy remains protected and may not be used for another purpose.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 22 already delivers our preferred audit position in full:

- **Frequency:** no more than once in any twelve-month period (22.1)
- **Notice:** at least thirty days' prior written notice (22.1)
- **Manner:** normal business hours, no unreasonable disruption, off-site where practicable, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality (22.1)
- **Cost:** Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds five percent for the audited period (22.2)
- **System access:** express prohibition on Vendor/auditor accessing our systems directly, unrelated Customer Data, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information (22.2)

Section 22.3 adds further protections in our favour (findings are our Confidential Information, use limited to enforcement, copy of the final report, and finality on payment of a shortfall absent fraud or demonstrable error).

Section 23 ("Records and Customer Assurance") is a heading with no operative text, so it does not extend any audit right, and a document-wide search surfaced no other audit, inspection, or verification rights binding us.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

paragraphs.text: 7. FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES

7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.

7.2 Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.

7.3 Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.

7.4 Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.

7.5 Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.
7.6 Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms.

7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
4. ORDER FORMS AND AFFILIATE ORDERS

4.1 An Order Form becomes binding when signed by both Parties. Changes in scope, assumptions, quantities, Fees, dependencies, or dates require a written change order signed by authorized representatives. Vendor shall not charge for work outside scope that Customer did not approve in a signed change order.

"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.

Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

paragraphs.text: 10. EFFECT OF EXPIRY OR TERMINATION

10.1 On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.

10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.
15. CUSTOMER DATA AND PRIVACY

15.1 Vendor shall process Customer Data only on Customer's documented instructions, to provide the Services, and as permitted by this Agreement. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data, use it for advertising, combine it with another customer's identifiable data, or train a generally available model on it without Customer's express written consent.

15.2 Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law concerning personal information. If Vendor processes personal information for Customer, the Parties' data-processing addendum is incorporated. Vendor is a processor or service provider and shall assist Customer with data-subject requests, impact assessments, consultations, and regulatory inquiries.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.

Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.

Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.

Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).

Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

paragraphs.text: 8. TERM AND RENEWAL

8.1 This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms. Expiration of this Agreement does not itself terminate an Order Form then in effect; this Agreement continues to govern that Order Form until the Order Form expires or is terminated.

8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.

8.3 On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 19 satisfies the WARRANTY rule at or above the preferred position:

- **19.1** — professional and workmanlike performance by qualified personnel to industry standards, plus material conformity of Services and Deliverables to documentation and specifications.
- **19.2** — 90 days for Deliverables, measured from the *later* of delivery or acceptance (favourable tolling), and Hosted Services conform *throughout the subscription term* — full-term coverage for the software element, better than the 12-month preferred benchmark for a hosted model.
- **19.3** — no malicious code, compliance with Applicable Law, no functionality diminution, and an open-source/source-code-contamination warranty.
- **19.4** — re-perform/repair/replace at no charge, with termination and refund of Fees as a backstop; remedy is expressly *non-exclusive* for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. This is stronger than our model language, which leaves the remedy choice with Vendor.
- **19.5** — the only disclaimer is mutual, limited to implied warranties, and expressly states that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy. The disclaimer therefore does not swallow the express warranty, and there is no "AS IS" language anywhere in the document.

Neither the acceptance regime (6.1–6.2) nor the performance clause (3.1) cuts the warranty short: acceptance adds a correction-cycle and refund right rather than displacing the warranty, and silence or productive use does not constitute acceptance.

input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer to Vendor for late payment, which the playbook prohibits. The amount (15% of annual Fees per week of delay) is punitive and would rapidly exceed the remaining contract value, putting it in walk-away territory; it also sits uneasily with the dispute-withholding right in 7.3 and the mutual liability cap in 21.1 (which expressly does not limit Fee obligations). No Customer-payable early-termination or minimum fee appears elsewhere (Sections 9 and 21 are clean), so the single fix is to strike the LD and substitute ordinary late-payment interest as Vendor's sole remedy.

We are happy to discuss the interest rate or a modest fixed late fee if that helps.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.

No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.

Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.

Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.

Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer to Vendor for late payment, which the playbook prohibits. The amount (15% of annual Fees per week of delay) is punitive and would rapidly exceed the remaining contract value, putting it in walk-away territory; it also sits uneasily with the dispute-withholding right in 7.3 and the mutual liability cap in 21.1 (which expressly does not limit Fee obligations). No Customer-payable early-termination or minimum fee appears elsewhere (Sections 9 and 21 are clean), so the single fix is to strike the LD and substitute ordinary late-payment interest as Vendor's sole remedy.

paragraphs.text: 9. TERMINATION

9.1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail. If a breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, the cure period extends up to sixty additional days while the breaching Party diligently pursues cure.

9.2 Either Party may terminate immediately by written notice if the other becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for creditors, enters liquidation, or becomes subject to a bankruptcy proceeding not dismissed within sixty days. A lawful reorganization that does not impair performance is not, by itself, grounds for termination.

9.3 Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.

9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.

9.5 Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity) at § 7.7 (p0032).**

- **Issue:** Section 7.7 requires Customer to pay Vendor "as liquidated damages and not as a penalty" 15% of *annual* Fees for *each week* an invoice is unpaid after a 10-day grace period. This is a Customer-payable LD, which the playbook prohibits outright, and the quantum is punitive enough to exceed the remaining contract value within weeks (walk-away territory).
- **Context checked:** No Customer-payable early-termination or minimum fee exists elsewhere — § 9.4 confirms Customer owes only accrued Fees on termination for convenience, § 27 termination is "without penalty," and § 21 contains no penalty language. § 7.3 gives us a withholding right for disputed amounts that 7.7 would undercut, and § 21.3 confirms Fee obligations sit outside the liability cap.
- **Redline (validated, preferred):** Strike the LD and substitute ordinary simple late-payment interest (lesser of 1%/month or the legal maximum) as Vendor's sole remedy, limited to proper, undisputed invoices with a 30-day grace period, plus an express statement that Customer owes no liquidated damages or penalties.

**Finding: compliant — no redline proposed.**

Section 18 (¶¶ p0074–p0075) already satisfies the INSURANCE rule in full:

| Preferred position | Document (§ 18.1) |
|---|---|
| CGL USD 1M/occ, 2M agg | ✅ Matches exactly |
| Professional / E&O USD 2M | ✅ Matches exactly |
| Cyber/privacy USD 5M (Customer Data) | ✅ Matches; warranted since Vendor hosts and processes Customer Data (§§ 15, 17) |
| Workers' comp as required by law | ✅ Plus employer's liability USD 1M (extra) |
| Certificates on request | ✅ § 18.2 |

The clause also exceeds our position on several points in our favor: the term-plus-one-year duration tracks our model language, and § 18.2 adds reputable-insurer and primary-coverage requirements, advance notice of cancellation or material reduction, and an express statement that insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities — which preserves our recovery under the indemnity and liability provisions (§§ 20, 21).

The obligation runs entirely against Brightline (Vendor) and benefits us, so there is nothing to push back on. No fallback discussion needed.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement affirmatively takes our preferred position:

- **§ 2.1 (p0013):** "No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies," Customer pays only for Services ordered under an executed Order Form, and declining to enter another Order Form "is not a breach or shortfall."
- **§ 12.3 (p0051):** Confirms Customer has made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer or **minimum-volume** commitment.
- **§ 7.1 (p0026):** Bars Vendor from imposing any platform, support, administration or **minimum-use** charge not identified in the Order Form.

I also checked the planner's candidate sections: § 4 (Order Forms) has no committed quantities or non-reducible seat counts; § 7 has no take-or-pay or shortfall true-up; § 8.2 renews Order Forms only in twelve-month increments with a Customer-side thirty-day non-renewal right (plus a reminder-dependent extension), so there is no multi-year lock-in. The only "shortfall" references (§ 22.1–22.2) relate to Vendor's licence audit of actual usage, not a purchase commitment, and so do not engage this rule.

One item outside this rule's scope, flagged for the record: § 7.7 (p0032) imposes "liquidated damages" of 15% of *annual* Fees per week for late payment — an unenforceable-looking penalty on us that should be addressed under the late-payment/interest rule.
Section 11 squarely delivers the preferred position, and Sections 9, 10, and 15 contain no conflicting deletion or withholding terms.

input.quote: 11.1 Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form. Assistance includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, orderly migration, and continued service at the then-current scope and service levels.
input.rationale: Section 11 meets or exceeds the preferred position on all three elements. (a) Transition assistance: 11.1 gives Customer up to six months of assistance on request, priced at the rates in the expiring Order Form — more favourable to us than the playbook's "then-current rates" — and expressly includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, migration, and continued service at existing scope and service levels. (b) Data return: 11.2 requires return of all Customer Data within thirty days in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format with relationships and metadata, and bars Vendor from holding data hostage over a fee dispute. (c) Deletion and certification: 11.3 sequences deletion only after Customer confirms successful return, limits any retained copy to what Applicable Law requires (protected and use-restricted), and requires written certification by an authorized officer. Cross-checks show no conflict: Section 10.1 preserves Customer Data rights and ends access only after any agreed transition period; Section 15 restricts Vendor's processing; the definition of Customer Data (1.3) is broad; and no suspension, termination (Section 9), or other clause permits immediate deletion or withholding. No redline needed.

Assistance includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, orderly migration, and continued service at the then-current scope and service levels.
input.rationale: Section 11 meets or exceeds the preferred position on all three elements. (a) Transition assistance: 11.1 gives Customer up to six months of assistance on request, priced at the rates in the expiring Order Form — more favourable to us than the playbook's "then-current rates" — and expressly includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, migration, and continued service at existing scope and service levels. (b) Data return: 11.2 requires return of all Customer Data within thirty days in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format with relationships and metadata, and bars Vendor from holding data hostage over a fee dispute. (c) Deletion and certification: 11.3 sequences deletion only after Customer confirms successful return, limits any retained copy to what Applicable Law requires (protected and use-restricted), and requires written certification by an authorized officer. Cross-checks show no conflict: Section 10.1 preserves Customer Data rights and ends access only after any agreed transition period; Section 15 restricts Vendor's processing; the definition of Customer Data (1.3) is broad; and no suspension, termination (Section 9), or other clause permits immediate deletion or withholding. No redline needed.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 11 ("Transition Assistance and Data Return") already satisfies the preferred position in full:

| Playbook element | Document |
|---|---|
| Transition assistance up to 6 months at then-current rates | § 11.1 — six months on Customer's request, at the rates in the **expiring Order Form** (better than preferred, since it locks pricing rather than exposing us to rate increases); includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, migration, and continued service at existing scope/SLAs |
| Return of Customer Data within 30 days in machine-readable format | § 11.2 — thirty days, "complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format," with relationships and metadata; plus an express bar on withholding data over a fee dispute |
| Deletion certified thereafter | § 11.3 — deletion only *after* Customer confirms successful return, legal-retention copies remain protected and purpose-limited, and an authorized officer certifies deletion in writing |

Cross-checks confirmed no clause undercuts this: § 10.1 preserves Customer Data rights and ends access only after the transition period; § 9 contains no immediate-deletion or data-forfeiture trigger; § 15 constrains Vendor's processing; and the § 1.3 definition of Customer Data is appropriately broad (excluding only unlinkable telemetry).

Two points are worth noting as favourable deviations we should preserve if the counterparty proposes edits: the fee-dispute non-withholding sentence in 11.2 and the return-before-deletion sequencing in 11.3.
